html:
Prussian statesman who united Germany through three short wars and served as its first chancellor from 1871 to 1890.

A conservative landowner, he became chief minister of Prussia in 1862. He said the great questions of the day would be settled not by speeches but by "iron and blood". Then he won three wars:

  • against Denmark in 1864, over Schleswig and Holstein;
  • against Austria in 1866, which pushed Austria out of German affairs;
  • against France in 1870 and 1871, the Franco-Prussian War.

In January 1871 Wilhelm I was proclaimed German emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. The Zollverein customs union had already tied the German states together.

As chancellor he kept the peace in Europe with a web of alliances and hosted the Berlin Conference on Africa. At home he fought the Catholic Church and the socialists, but also created the first state health, accident and old age insurance, to win workers away from socialism. The young emperor Wilhelm II dismissed him in 1890.
sum: Prussian statesman who united Germany through three short wars and served as its first chancellor from 1871 to 1890.
